Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

stadium noun

also sports ground, arena, football stadium, amphitheatre, amphitheater

classical

Cic. Off. 3.42; Tusc. 2.56
Vitr. 5.11.4 (M-O)
Traupman 45, 50, 174

stadium, stadiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Classically the Greek running track and the ground round it, where hominum cōpiae cum laxāmentō āthlētās certantēs spectāre could watch the athletes (Vitr. 5.11.4, as Morgan–Owens quotes it); also a measure of length, a stade.

Other words

  • amphitheātrum, amphitheātrī n. — an arena, a large round stadium

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. arena, stadium; Traupman 173; Traupman 271 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The Roman arena, built all round for shows; a covered sports arena is amphitheātrum tēctum (Morgan–Owens).

  • arēna (harēna), arēnae f. — the arena, the sanded floor of an amphitheatre

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. harēna; Traupman 272 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • ut in stadiō cursōrēs exclāmant

    as runners shout out on the trackCic. Tusc. 2.56 (Lewis & Short)

  • stadium pedifollī

    a football stadiumTraupman 50

  • stadium pedifolliī

    a soccer stadiumTraupman 382

See also pitch, race, sport.
